A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ShadowKV. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracy, A100 throughput measurements, and ablation results in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, precision tests, scalability experiments, and component analyses in Section 5 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: v1 describes compressing newly generated keys but explicitly excludes it from the implementation. v2 implements and evaluates this extension as ShadowKV+, reusing the prefill projections (Section 4.1, Appendix A.1). The base ShadowKV algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The benchmark and task families remain unchanged, including InfiniteBench already present in v1's appendix. v2 extends RULER's tested input conditions to 512K and 1M contexts (Appendix A.5), beyond v1's 128K main evaluation and MInference experiments through 256K.

E2.justification: InfiniGen, previously discussed but not evaluated, and its value-only variant join the RULER and LongBench comparisons across all four original models (Table 1, Appendix A.3). Quest also becomes an explicit throughput comparator in Table 14; v1's throughput comparison used full attention.

E3.justification: v2 adds FP8 evaluation, Llama-3-70B-1M, expanded batch-size and context-length sweeps, operation-level timing experiments, and a batch-three, 1M-context offloading comparison. These substantially expand the evaluation design. The original default rank, chunk size, outlier count, and benchmark filtering remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test generated-key compression, FP8 sensitivity, outlier counts from zero to 48, scaling, and prefill/decoding latency contributions (Appendix A). These directly examine previously untested components and operating conditions. The original budget, rank, and chunk-size analyses remain, although the detailed chunk-size versus hit-rate panel is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or an uncertainty-estimation procedure. The additional results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: The original tabulated RULER, LongBench, MInference, throughput, and InfiniteBench scores are retained after matching relocated content. v2 adds extensive results for the new comparisons and analyses; Table 14 reports 45.32 tokens/s for ShadowKV versus 9.34 for Quest with CPU offloading at 3×1M. Figure 1 also reports substantially lower SVD overhead without explaining the revision, so it does not establish a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a GPU-memory-savings expression and a worked 7.08× example. The subspace-similarity definition, its bounds, and the equivalent-bandwidth derivation remain unchanged. The new expression omits the M factor from its sparse/outlier term, unlike Section 4.2's byte accounting.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central accuracy, 6× batch-size, and 3.04× throughput claims. The introduction adds an explicit claim of higher accuracy than approaches applying low-rank approximations to weights, sharpening the comparative claim without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix A.8 connects the first outlier chunk to attention sinks and adds a specific qualification: inadequate outlier handling can make mean-based landmarks worse than Quest's min-max selection. v2 also interprets the new FP8 tests as precision robustness and expands explanations of its advantages over InfiniGen.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 newly discloses BF16 weights and KV caches for the main experiments and specifies torch.float8_e5m2 for the additional FP8 tests. The implementation framework, kernel descriptions, default hyperparameters, and repository address are otherwise retained in Appendix B.1.

R1.justification: v2 expands the distinction from the already-cited InfiniGen, especially its offline selection projections versus ShadowKV's prompt-dependent compression. It adds references including MatryoshkaKV, Eigen Attention, and Effectively Compress KV Heads for LLM, while removing several general application citations. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain recognizable. v2 clarifies sparse budgets and temporal locality, revises selected paragraphs and author information, and separates additional results into Appendix A while moving the former experiment-details appendix to Appendix B.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the single-column main text with a substantially redesigned two-column layout. It merges the main accuracy tables, moves Yi results to the appendix, splits the original overview figure, adds a scheduling diagram and numerous tables, and removes the detailed prefill/decoding illustrations and chunk-hit-rate panel.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support by addressing v1's missing InfiniGen evaluation, directly testing the importance of outliers, and providing operation-level latency evidence. Generated-token compression, FP8, and larger-model tests further establish applicability. The unexplained SVD-plot revision, inconsistent new memory formula, and denser tables are drawbacks, but they do not outweigh the stronger validation of the central system claims.
